clue.text: Supports dictator's party, perhaps a little way

parts.note: supports, as a verb, means backs

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates, speaking words aloud, so the word for party is given as it sounds

parts.note: a party or outing can be a treat

explanation.surface: A dictator's party is backed, and it all happens down some little way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator's' is the sound signal: someone dictating says TREAT, which is heard as TREET. 'Dictator' wants to be a tyrant, but here it is just a person speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A back street is a minor road away from the main thoroughfare, an example of a little way.

clue.text: Impact one expects to have?

definitions.meaning: a woman who is expecting a baby shows a swelling at the belly

explanation.surface: An impact is something one expects to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is both a collision and the slang for a pregnant woman's swollen belly.

clue.text: Fenland river god duly uncovered a flower

parts.note: the Cam flows through Cambridge in the Fens
Pan is the Greek god of shepherds

indicators.note: with its cover taken off, the word duly loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A Fenland river god duly reveals a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are the flat marshy country of eastern England around Cambridge. 'uncovered' strips duly to UL.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanula is the bellflower genus, a garden bloom with bell-shaped petals.

clue.text: Two ways to rank second bank's services

parts.note: standing and order are two words that each mean a ranking or position

explanation.surface: Two ways to rank the second bank's services, as if comparing lenders.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'two ways' are the two words STANDING and ORDER, both ranking terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing orders are regular automatic payments a bank makes on a customer's instruction.

clue.text: Recoils from victory secured by Left

indicators.note: held firm inside, so the word for victory sits within the word for left

parts.note: Reds are left-wingers, so the Left can be the Reds
a victory is a win

explanation.surface: Someone recoils from a victory the political Left has secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recoils' looks like flinching, but it is coils again, as with a tape.
explanation.definitionFit: To rewind is to wind back or coil up again, so it recoils in the literal sense.

clue.text: Capricious sailor turning up in Morecambe, say

indicators.note: placed inside, so the turned word sits within the name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a famous British comedian, so Morecambe is an example of an Eric

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A fickle sailor shows up in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a Lancashire resort, but here it is the comedian Eric Morecambe. 'turning up' reverses TAR to RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricious and erratic both describe behaviour that is unpredictable and changeable.

clue.text: Unlikely score Yankee discounted

indicators.note: something discounted is taken off, so the letter for Yankee is removed

parts.note: a tally is a score or count
Y is Yankee in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An unlikely score with the Yankees left out of the count.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story or tall order is improbable or hard to believe.

clue.text: Well-briefed army leader fighting English

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: fighting is war

explanation.surface: An army leader well briefed for the fighting with the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-briefed has been informed and so knows what is going on.

clue.text: Line you are splitting to once again do hand-outs

indicators.note: splitting a word means going into the middle of it

parts.note: to iterate is to do again
UR is text-speak for you are

explanation.surface: A line on handing things out again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature can mean printed leaflets or brochures, the printed matter given out to the public.

clue.text: Juliet has long excited eminent novelist

parts.note: J is Juliet in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: an eminent person is a worthy

explanation.surface: Juliet has long been excited by an eminent novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: He wrote The Forsyte Saga and won the Nobel Prize for Literature.

clue.text: Baby initially nursed by two parents, one with fangs

indicators.note: held in the arms, so the letter sits inside the parents

parts.note: MA and MA, two mothers

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of a word

explanation.surface: A baby nursed by two parents, one of whom has fangs.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a venomous African snake, so it has fangs.

clue.text: Two sent off outside ark for renewed creation

indicators.note: one group of letters goes round the other
sent off in all directions, so these letters are scattered
made anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people sent off from the ark when it is rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ark' tempts a biblical reading, but it is plain fodder; 'sent off' and 'renewed' are two separate anagram signals, one wrapping round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A work of art is something an artist has made, a creation.

clue.text: Bond hero putting on weight, heading for bar during conference?

parts.note: padding is putting on bulk or filling
a ton is a weight

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: being in conference with someone is having their ear, a private word in it

explanation.surface: James Bond gaining weight and heading for the bar during a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' wants to be James Bond; it is Michael Bond, the children's author. The question mark flags the loose sense of EAR for a hearing in conference.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington Bear is the marmalade-loving bear from Michael Bond's children's books.

clue.text: Panels assembled to provide lodging after game

indicators.note: comes after in the answer, so the lodging word follows the game word

parts.note: a match is a game
board is lodging, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Panels put together to give a place to stay after the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchboard is tongue-and-groove boarding, planks fitted together to form panelling.

clue.text: Former student record disheartened their association

indicators.note: losing its heart, the word for record drops its middle letter

parts.note: an album is a record
the NUS, National Union of Students, is students' association

explanation.surface: A former student's record of their union association, rather downhearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' refers back to students: the NUS is the UK National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a graduate or past pupil of a school or college.

clue.text: Ring for the head, boy needing permit

parts.note: a chap is a boy or fellow
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A boy needs a permit to wear a ring on his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a garland or wreath worn on the head.

clue.text: The setter's penetrating clues cryptically shed light

indicators.note: going into, so the setter's word sits inside the jumbled letters
read cryptically, the letters are disguised in a new order

parts.note: the setter's means belonging to me, mine

explanation.surface: The setter's insight into clues sheds light on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptically' turns CLUES into LUSCE, which MINE goes into.
explanation.definitionFit: To luminesce is to give off light without heat, so to shed light.

clue.text: Outcry about "Love in Paris"

parts.note: C is circa, about
l'amour is French for love

explanation.surface: A public outcry over love in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud protest or noisy demand, an outcry.

clue.text: Author ditching wife, claiming unknown one's posher

indicators.note: taking hold of, so the other letters go inside
dropping, so the letter for wife goes

parts.note: a writer is an author
Z is an algebraic unknown
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An author ditches his wife and claims an unknown woman is classier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditching' removes W from WRITER to give RITER, which takes in ZI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritzy means luxurious and smart, after the Ritz hotel, so ritzier is more upmarket.

clue.text: Far side of oak tree backing border state

indicators.note: the far side of a word is its last letter

parts.note: an ash is a tree

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: The far side of an oak tree backs onto a state border.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmir is a region and former princely state in the north of the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Most ardent laments in Shakespeare's time?

definitions.meaning: the old second-person form, thou mournest, of the verb keen, to wail for the dead

explanation.surface: The most passionate laments date from Shakespeare's era.
explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief, and Elizabethan English added -est for thou; it is also the superlative of eager.

clue.text: Bishop heeds petition condemned as irrelevant

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: condemned letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A bishop pays attention to a petition but dismisses it as irrelevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beside the point is off-topic, having no bearing on the matter.

clue.text: Bar close to outfield reserved

parts.note: bar, meaning except, is save

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A bar near the outfield is reserved, as at a cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Saved and reserved both mean kept back for later use.

clue.text: Complaint, women's trouble

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A complaint about women's trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A wail is a cry of protest or grievance, a complaint.

clue.text: Promote retro technology, in hostile environment

indicators.note: placed inside, so the reversed letters sit within

parts.note: a hostile environment is an adverse one

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Promoting retro technology in an unfriendly market.
explanation.definitionFit: To advertise a product is to publicise it to boost sales, to promote it.

clue.text: Inventor with unit in institute's lab

indicators.note: the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: An inventor and his unit at work in the institute's laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was an inventor, and the SI unit of magnetic flux density is named after him.

clue.text: Pop round to see a wall panel

parts.note: pop is dad, father
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Dad pops round to look at a wall panel.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower part of an interior wall, decorated differently from the upper.

clue.text: Roughly one drop of rain in paltry fountain

indicators.note: placed inside the word for paltry

parts.note: petty means paltry or trivial

indicators.note: a single drop of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a well is a fountain or source

explanation.surface: Roughly one drop of rain lands in a feeble fountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty well means more or less, almost, which is what roughly means.
